sentences.text: Since both these Petitions arise out of the same accident and in view of the Order dated 0804 2022 in MVC.No.5902/2019, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 11082019 at about 1.45 a.m. the petitioner in 5902/2019 was riding motor cycle bearing No.05HL1519, along with the deceased Suman Mondal in MVC.5903/2019, as pillion rider.

When they reached CISF junction, Airport new road, KIAL Bangalore, at that time, one Innova car bearing No.KA52M6055 came from back side of the motor cycle, the driver of said car driven the said vehicle at a high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler.
Due to the said impact, petitioner and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, Petitioner in 5902/2019 was shifted to Astra hospital,
Devanahalli for first aid and then shifted to CMI Astra hospital, Hebbal wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
Later, he was shifted to St.Ignatius Hospital, Honavar wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

Immediately after the accident, deceased Suman Mondal in MVC.5903/2019 was shifted to Astra hospital, Devanahalli for first aid and then shifted to CMI Astra hospital, Hebbal wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and succumbed to the injuries on 12.08.2019.
4.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.No.5902/2019 was hale and healthy and was working as cook and earning Rs.30,000/p.m.

5. Prior to the date of accident, the deceased Suman Mondal in MVC.5903/2019 was hale and healthy and he was working as cook and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
6.

The Petitioners of both the Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA 52M6055 which is owned by the Respondent No.1 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such, both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in both petitions, the Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed detailed Objection Statement.
In both the petitions, Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and of the petitioner in 5902/2019.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and Shafali Mondal vs Hemanth Murthy.
N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187672699/
3 negligent driving of the offending Innova car by its driver.
Further it contended that the driver of the Innova car was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the Innova car.

Further it contended that the owner of the Innova car knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid driving licence has entrusted the said vehicle to him and has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the deceased and Petitioner in both the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
Further it contended that the accident took place due to negligence of the rider of two wheeler and the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Further contended that there is contributory negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.
8. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.
ISSUES IN MVC NO.5902/2019 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 1108 2019 at about 1.45 a.m. at CISF junction, Airport New Road, KIAL,
Bangalore, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Innova car bearing No.KA52M6055 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award ?
ISSUES IN MVC NO.5903/2019 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that Sri.Suman Mondal S/o Pravat Mondal was died in the Road Traffic Accident which occurred on 11.08.2019 at about 1.45 a.m., at CISF junction, Airport New Road, KIAL, Bangalore, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Innova car bearing No.KA52 M6055 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of Suman Mondal?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4. What Order or Award ?
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner in MVC.5902/2019 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
The petitioner No.2 in 5903/2019 got examined himself as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P13 to 18.
PW.1 and 2 got examined two witnesses as PW.3 and PW.4 and got marked Ex.P.19 to 29 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.

I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and of the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

11. My answer to the Issues in MVC No.5902/2019 are as under :
 Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
12.

My answer to the Issues in MVC.5903/2019 are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 13. Issue No.1 in MVC.5902/2019 and 5903/2019:

It is the case of the Petitioners that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Innova car bearing No.KA52 M6055 by its driver and in the said accident, petitioner in 5902/2019 sustained grievous injuries.
And Suman Mondal had succumbed to the injuries.
14. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, Petitioner in MVC.5902/2019 has been examined as P.W.1 and petitioner No.2 in 5903/2019 got examined himself as P.W.2 and got marked Ex. P.1 to 18.

Ex. P1 to Ex.P6, Ex.P.13 and 14 are the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch, copy of notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Reply notice, Wound certificate,
Charge Sheet, PM report and Inquest report.

15. Upon going through the said documents, it shows that on the complaint lodged by the petitioner in MVC.5902/2019, the case was registered against the driver of the offending Innova car bearing No.KA52M6055 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
The documents Ex.P.3 justify the fact of involvement of vehicles bearing Reg.No.KA05HL1519 and KA52M6055 in the accident.
The document Ex. P2 justify the fact that in the presence of pancha witnesses IO has conducted the procedure of spot mahazar.
Ex. P.5
is the wound certificate justify the fact that petitioner in MVC.5902/2019 sustained grievous injuries.
Ex. P.14
justify the fact of death of Suman Mondal.
Moreover, Ex.P.13 discloses that the cause of death is due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained.
The prime document i.e., Ex. P.6 discloses the fact that IO after thorough investigation charge sheeted the driver of offending vehicle for the offences alleged punishable u/s 279, 338, 304A of IPC.

At this juncture it is to be noted that the Shafali Mondal vs Hemanth Murthy.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187672699/
5 charge sheet allegations do not support the contention of respondent No.2 with regard to the allegation that the driver of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
16.
The documents Ex.P.7 and 8 are discharge summaries, Ex.P.9 is medical bills, Ex.P.10 is Advance bills, Ex. P.11 is the notarized copy of Aadhar cards.
Ex.P.12 is the notarized copy of Driving licence.

Ex.P.15 to 18 are the notarised copy of Aadhar card of Petitioners and of the deceased in 5903/2019.
17.

Further, PW.1 in MVC.5902/2019 has examined two witnesses as PW.3 and PW.4 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.19 to 29 i.e., Ex.P.19 is Clinical Examination report, Ex.P.20 Xray,
Ex.P.21 to 24 are pay slips of petitioner in MVC.5902/2019, Ex.P.25 is relieving letter and Experience certificate.
Ex.P.26 to 29 are pay slips of deceased Suman Mondal in MVC.5903/2019.
18. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1 to P.W.4, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross examined the P.W.1 to PW.4 at length.
In the crossexamination PW.1 to PW.4 have denied the suggestions and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the Petitioners.
19. In order to rebut the evidence of petitioners, respondents have not adduced any rebuttal evidence.
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
In addition to this, the documents Ex.P.5 justify the fact that as a result of occurrence of accident, the petitioner in 5902/2019 sustained injuries as mentioned in the said document.

20. The oral and documentary evidence of P.W.1 to PW.4 and the materials available on record,
clearly shows that the said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the said accident has been occurred as a result of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver and the Petitioner in 5902/2019 sustained grievous injuries and the deceased Suman Mondal in MVC.5903/2019 succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in MVC.5902/2019 and 5903/2019 in the "Affirmative".
21. Issue No. 2 in 5902/2019 :
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Innova car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22. It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.5 Wound Certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Right leg deformity present, crepitus present 2.
Radiograph of right thigh, Comminuted displaced fracture of mid shaft of femur noted.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the injuries are grievous in nature.

Shafali Mondal vs Hemanth Murthy.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187672699/
6 23.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 21 years.
He has produced aadhar card at Ex.P.11 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card, date of birth is shown as 19.11.1998.
The accident has taken place on 11.08.2019.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 21 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
24. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as cook and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/p.m.
In this regard, PW.4 has produced pay slips for the months of January 2019 to August 2019 to prove his avocation and income.
The documents produced at Ex.P.21 to 24 discloses the fact that one Clifford Lopes was drawing average salary of sum of Rs.20,000/.p.m.
The petitioner admittedly examined the HR of his company to prove the said documents.
The evidence deposed by PW.4 supports the documents Ex.P.21 to 24.
Though suggestions were made to PW.4 during cross examination that in order to help the claimants, the said documents have been concocted
, such suggestions are categorically denied by PW.4.
The document Ex. P.25 supports the case of petitioner that as a result of injuries sustained by him in the RTA, the petitioner could not continue his work.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is considered as monthly income of the petitioner.
25. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
26.
The petitioner has deposed that due to the injuries he cannot do his regular activities, cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier and he has become too weak.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
27.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30.000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
28.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 11 082019 to 16082019 at Aster CIM Hospital and from 2108 2019 to 24 082019 at St.Ignatius hospital.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 10 days.
29. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head (@ Rs.20,000/ per month).

7

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
30.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
31. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent Rs.4,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced 16 medical bills at Ex.P.9 amounting to Rs.2,66,253/.
I have perused the same carefully.
Careful perusal of Ex.P.9 justifies the fact that petitioner has furnished medical bills to a sum of Rs.2,66,253/.

The document Ex.P.10 is the advance receipts for a sum of Rs.1,50,000/
.
During cross examination of PW.1 there is no serious dispute made regarding the medical bills.
However, the payments made vide advance receipts shall be deducted from the total claim of medical expenses.

As such from Rs.2,66,253/ a sum of Rs.1,50,000/is deducted and the petitioner is entitled for claim of medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,16,253/ which is rounded off to Rs.1,16,300/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION
TOWARDS
PERMANENT DISABILITY :
32. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he was forced to resign his job.

To substantiate this fact,
petitioner relied upon the document at Ex. P.25.
In addition to this, he also got examined PW.4 to support his assertion.

If careful consideration is given to the evidence given by PW.1 and PW.4 along with documents placed on hand in that regard, they justify the fact that as per Ex.P.25, the petitioner was relieved from his employment with effect from 10.09.2019.

33. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N. as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical examination report and Xray at Ex.P.19 and 20.
He assessed total disability of his whole body at 18% and the disability of right lower limb at 53%.
34. In the crossexamination PW.3 has stated that he has not personally treated the petitioner at any point of time.
He has admitted the suggestion that he has not referred any other documents except wound certificate and the discharge summary.
There is also admission of the fact that no estimation has been given by him in respect of removal of implants.
He has denied the suggestion that he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

35. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on hand and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, upon consideration of the fact Shafali Mondal vs Hemanth Murthy.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187672699/
8 that the petitioner got examined himself before this court as PW.1 and also tendered for cross examination done at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2 during which he could be able to give rational answers to the questions and regarding the facts of the case and considering all these aspects, this Tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable if the disability of the Petitioner is considered at 10%.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.20,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,32,000/ (Rs.20,000/ x 12 = 2,40,000/, Rs.2.40,000/x 18 x 10/100 = 4,32,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,32,000/ under this head.
36. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he needs future medical expenses.

However, in the evidence he has stated that he needs sum of Rs.1,00,000/
for future medical expenses as he needs to undergo surgery for removal of implants.
The witness PW.3 during his evidence estimated that petitioner requires sum of Rs.60,000/ for removal of implants.
In the absence of any estimation/document this Tribunal is of the view that if Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head, it would be just and reasonable.
Hence, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
37.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3.
Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.1,16,300/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 40,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.4,32,000/
7.
Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/ Total Rs.6,96,300/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,96,300/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
38. Issue No.2 & 3 in MVC.5903/2019
: Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are inter linked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.

9 39.
The Petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are parents of the deceased and petitioner No.4 is younger sister of deceased Suman Mondal.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.2 has produced Aadhar cards of the Petitioners and of the deceased at Ex.P15 to 18.
The said documents justify the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
Same also justify that the petitioners and the deceased Suman Mondal were residing together .
Hence, the Petitioners are considered as the L.Rs of deceased Suman Mondal, they are entitled for the compensation.
40. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 24 years and he was working as cook in hotel and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
In this regard, petitioners have examined the HR Manager of deceased as PW.4.
PW.4 has produced pay slips of the deceased for the month of May 2019 to August 2019.
On careful consideration of the said documents, same discloses that on an average, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.27,000/p.m.
Though PW.4 was subjected for cross examination at length, the veracity of evidence given by him in respect of the documents stood unshaken.

Accordingly, income of deceased is considered at Rs.27,000/p.m.
41.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Suman Mondal was 24 years at the time of the accident.
PW.2 has produced Ex.P.18 i.e., Aadhar Card of the deceased.
As per Ex.P.18, the date of birth is shown as 1701 1994.
The alleged accident was occurred on 11082019.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Suman Mondal was 25 years.
Hence, the age of the deceased Suman Mondal to be taken at 25 years for the purpose of assessment.
42. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
43.
The deceased has left behind his wife, parents and sister.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are parents and Petitioner No.4 is sister of the deceased and they are considered as dependents of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that :
"Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/ and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/".

, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rupees 44,000/ each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
44.

Petitioner No.1 is the wife and she lost her husband's love and care and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are parents have lost their son's love and care and petitioner No.4 is the sister of deceased and she has lost brother's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/ collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.
Accordingly, the same is awarded.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
45.
The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/ collectively under this head would be just and reasonable.
Accordingly, the same is awarded.

VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:
46.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased to be taken at Rs.27,000/ pm.
47.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :

48.

The decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "In case self employed or person on fixed salary the addition should be 40% when the age is below 40 years".

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Petition, the deceased was aged 25 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.27,000/ comes to Rs.10,800/.
Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.37,800/ p.m. (Rs.27,000/ + Rs.10,800/).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 18.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

49. After deducting 1/4th towards his personal expenses in Rs.37,800/ it comes to Rs.28,350/
(Rs.37,800/  9,450/) and multiplier applied is 18 which comes to Rs.61,23,600/ (28,350 x 12 x 18).

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.61,23,600/ which is rounded off to Rs.61,23,600/ towards loss of dependency.
50.

3. Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 16,500/
5. Transportation of dead body Rs. 10,000/
5. Loss of Dependency Rs.61,23,600/ Total Rs.63,92,600/

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.63,92,600/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
